# The `clickhouse` source (package `clickhouse`)

This reference covers `clickhouse` versions `>=1.0.1, <2.0.0`. Compare with the version
`dre plugin list` shows (in a project, `dre.lock` pins it); outside that range, say its
options may differ from this list before relying on it.

## Profile fields

A `profiles.yml` target under `sources:` with `type: clickhouse` takes these fields.
Never write a secret's value: use `env_var()` (SEC-3).

| Field | Required | Secret | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `driver` | no | no | `http` | the protocol: http (the default) or native, ClickHouse's own TCP protocol |
| `host` | no | no | `localhost` | server host name |
| `port` | no | no |  | server port (default 8123, 8443 with secure, 9000 native, 9440 native with secure) |
| `user` | no | no | `default` | user name |
| `password` | no | yes |  | password |
| `schema` | no | no | `default` | the ClickHouse database to use (dbt's name; `database` also works) |
| `secure` | no | no | `false` | connect with TLS (ClickHouse Cloud needs it) |
| `verify` | no | no | `true` | check the server's TLS certificate |
| `ca_cert` | no | no |  | CA certificate to trust for the server's TLS certificate (PEM), when it isn't from a public CA |
| `client_cert` | no | no |  | client certificate (PEM), for mutual TLS |
| `client_cert_key` | no | no |  | the client certificate's private key (PEM) |
| `server_host_name` | no | no |  | the host name to expect on the server's TLS certificate, when it isn't `host` |
| `connect_timeout` | no | no | `10s` | how long to wait for a connection (`30s`, `2m`, or seconds) |
| `send_receive_timeout` | no | no | `300s` | how long to wait on a read or write to the server (`5m`, or seconds) |
| `compression` | no | no |  | how results are compressed on the wire: lz4 (the default), zstd, none, or for http gzip, deflate or br |
| `custom_settings` | no | no |  | ClickHouse settings for every query, e.g. max_execution_time: 300 |
| `retries` | no | no | `3` | how many times to try connecting again after a temporary error (0: never) |
| `ssh` | no | yes |  | reach the server through an SSH bastion (a block of settings) |

## Report options

None: a source's settings are its profile fields.

## From the plugin docs

### ClickHouse

#### Notes

Field names and values are dbt-clickhouse's, so a dbt profile can be copied across: `schema`
names the ClickHouse database (`database` also works, and must match `schema` when both are set).
The fields dbt-clickhouse only uses to build models (`cluster`, `database_engine`,
`use_lw_deletes`, `local_suffix`, ...) are accepted and ignored.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `driver` | `http` (the default) or `native`, ClickHouse's own TCP protocol. HTTP sessions survive a failed statement; see below. |
| `host`, `port` | The port follows `driver` and `secure` unless set: 8123, 8443 with `secure`, 9000 native, 9440 native with `secure`. |
| `user`, `password` | `default` and no password unless set. |
| `schema` | The database unqualified table names are read from (default `default`). |
| `secure`, `verify` | TLS, and whether the server's certificate is checked (default yes). |
| `ca_cert` | A CA certificate (PEM) to trust, for a server whose certificate isn't from a public CA. |
| `client_cert`, `client_cert_key` | Mutual TLS. |
| `server_host_name` | The name to expect on the server's certificate, when it isn't `host` (a tunnel, an IP address). |
| `connect_timeout`, `send_receive_timeout` | Defaults `10s` and `300s`; a duration or seconds. |
| `compression` | `lz4` (the default), `zstd` or `none`; over HTTP also `gzip`, `deflate` or `br`. |
| `custom_settings` | ClickHouse settings sent with every query, e.g. `max_execution_time`, `max_memory_usage`. |
| `retries` | How many times to try connecting again after a temporary error (default 3). |
| `ssh` | Reach the server through an SSH bastion, with the [postgres source's settings](../docs/plugin-postgres.md). |

```yaml
connections:
  ch:
    targets:
      dev:        # a local server, e.g. clickhouse/clickhouse-server in Docker
        type: clickhouse
        user: default
        schema: analytics
      prod:       # ClickHouse Cloud
        type: clickhouse
        host: abc123.eu-west-1.aws.clickhouse.cloud
        secure: true
        user: dre_reader
        password: "{{ env_var('DRE_SECRET_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD') }}"
        schema: analytics
        custom_settings:
          max_execution_time: 300
```

Capabilities: `sessions`, `check`, `load`, `read_only`.

- **Sessions.** Every statement of a report's connection runs in one ClickHouse session, so a
  `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` or `SET` in a `tab: false` query is there for later tabs. Over HTTP
  that's a `session_id`. Over native it's one held connection, which ClickHouse closes after a
  failed statement: the temp tables and settings go with it, and the next statement says so.
- **check** (`dre validate --live`) runs `EXPLAIN`, which analyses a `SELECT` without running it.
  ClickHouse can only `EXPLAIN` a `SELECT`; any other statement is parsed (`EXPLAIN AST`), not
  analysed.
- **load** creates a temporary table on the session and sends the rows as one native insert.
- **Inlined lookups** spell `'` and `\` with backslashes, as ClickHouse reads them (it has no
  `chr()`, which other sources get). This needs DRE 0.5.1 and clickhouse 1.0.1; with an older
  DRE, give a lookup holding those characters `load: temp_table` in its YAML.
- **Read-only.** An unmanaged report's session runs with ClickHouse's `readonly = 2`: writes and
  DDL on tables are refused, `SET` and temp tables still work, and no statement can lower it.
  `dre query` uses `readonly = 1`, which also refuses `SET`, temp tables and the table functions
  that reach outside the database (`url`, `file`, `s3`, `remote`, ...). The profile's
  `custom_settings` apply either way.
- **Stopping a run** kills the running query on the server (`KILL QUERY` by its query ID), not
  only the request.

##### Types

ClickHouse follows the [rule every warehouse source follows](../docs/plugins.md#types-from-warehouses):

- `Nullable(T)`, `LowCardinality(T)` and `SimpleAggregateFunction(f, T)` read as `T`.
- Integers up to 64 bits are integers; `UInt64` is a `Decimal(20, 0)`, so it stays exact.
  `Int128`, `UInt128`, `Int256` and `UInt256` are exact text.
- `Decimal(P, S)` is a decimal up to 38 digits; wider is exact text.
- `Date` and `Date32` are dates. `DateTime` and `DateTime64` are UTC timestamps (ClickHouse stores
  instants), to the microsecond, or the nanosecond for `DateTime64(7)` to `(9)`.
- `Array`, `Tuple` (named: a JSON object in its declared order), `Map`, `Nested`, `JSON`,
  `Variant`, `Dynamic` and the geo types are compact JSON text on one line.
- `Enum` values are their names. `UUID`, `IPv4`, `IPv6`, intervals and `Time` (it can pass 24
  hours) are text. `FixedString` loses its NUL padding, and is hex when it isn't text.

The package is written in Go, on ClickHouse's official Go driver (`clickhouse-go`).

#### Try it locally

ClickHouse is open source, so a report can be tried against a server in Docker:

```bash
docker run -d -p 8123:8123 -p 9000:9000 -e CLICKHOUSE_USER=reports -e CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=reports-pass clickhouse/clickhouse-server
```

With `user: reports`, `password: "{{ env_var('DRE_SECRET_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD') }}"` and the
variable set to `reports-pass`, `select 1 as connection_check` in the [tutorial](https://github.com/get-dre/dre/blob/master/examples/tutorial/) project
checks the connection; `dre validate --live <report>` checks every statement before a run.

`invalid-connection-setting` needs the profile repaired before connecting. `connection-failed`
with "the port may be for the other protocol" means `driver` and `port` disagree (8123 and 8443
are HTTP; 9000 and 9440 native). See [profiles](../docs/reference-profiles.md),
[error codes](../docs/reference-error-codes.md), [connection](../docs/glossary.md#connection) and
[lookup](../docs/glossary.md#lookup).

### Types from warehouses

Every warehouse source (`databricks`, `bigquery`, `snowflake`, `clickhouse`) sends the same kinds
of value the same way, so a report looks the same whichever warehouse it reads (ClickHouse's own
types are on [its page](../docs/plugin-clickhouse.md#types)):

- Scalars keep their type. Exact numbers (`DECIMAL`, `NUMERIC`, `NUMBER(p,s)`) stay decimals at
  their declared precision; Snowflake `NUMBER(p,0)` up to 18 digits is an integer. Zone-aware
  timestamps (`TIMESTAMP`, `TIMESTAMP_TZ`/`_LTZ`) are UTC; naive ones (`TIMESTAMP_NTZ`,
  BigQuery `DATETIME`) stay naive.
- Semi-structured and nested values (`VARIANT`, `OBJECT`, `ARRAY`, `STRUCT`, `MAP`, `JSON`,
  BigQuery `RANGE`) become compact JSON text on one line, whatever the database returned. csv
  and `delimited` quote it like any other text, so a file never gets a line break in the middle
  of a record.
- Types no format holds exactly become text: intervals (Databricks' own text; BigQuery as ISO
  8601, e.g. `P1Y2M3DT4H`), geography and geometry, vectors, and `BIGNUMERIC` values wider than a
  38-digit decimal.
- A column of `NULL`s (`SELECT NULL`) is text.

xlsx refuses text longer than an Excel cell holds (32,767 characters): the run fails naming the
sheet, the cell and the column, rather than cutting the value. Shorten or cast it in the SQL, or
write that query to a text format.

## Guide notes

- Default to `driver: http`: its sessions survive a failed statement, so temp tables and `SET`
  from `tab: false` queries stay. Use `driver: native` only when the HTTP port isn't reachable.
- ClickHouse Cloud: `secure: true`, the service's host, a user and `password` from `env_var()`
  (SEC-2); the port follows `driver` and `secure` (8443 HTTP, 9440 native).
- A self-hosted server with a private CA: `ca_cert`; behind a bastion: `ssh` (the postgres
  source's settings). Never suggest `verify: false` except for a local test server.
- `schema` is the ClickHouse database. A copied dbt-clickhouse profile works as it is.
- For limits on agent or report queries, use `custom_settings` (`max_execution_time`,
  `max_memory_usage`, `max_result_rows`): they apply even in read-only sessions.
- To try ClickHouse locally, a `clickhouse/clickhouse-server` Docker container works.
